name: ACHIEVEAbility
statusReason: Active 501(c)(3) in West Philadelphia with ongoing housing and workforce programs; last 990 filed 2022 and 40th anniversary marked in 2021.
notes: Founded 1981 as Philadelphians Concerned About Housing (PCAH) by the Sisters of Mercy and women experiencing homelessness; renamed ACHIEVEability in 2003. In 2019 it formed a separate affiliate, ACHIEVEability Community Development Corporation. Pre-2017 executive directors not surfaced in available sources.

name: Chestnut Hill CDC
statusReason: Formed 2013, last 990 filed 2023, and still operating today (as the Chestnut Hill Business District, a City-registered community organization holding monthly meetings).
notes: Launched October 2013, funded by ~$850k of redirected Chestnut Hill Hospital business taxes over 10 years. Note: source currentExec listed Richard Snowden (President) — Snowden is a Chestnut Hill business figure/board-level role, not the staff ED; the ED succession (Sharkey -> Dawson -> O'Neill) is the operational leadership line. Exact Dawson departure and O'Neill start dates not confirmed.

name: Habitat for Humanity Philadelphia
statusReason: Operating 501(c)(3) with a current website, named leadership team, and ongoing build/repair programs; last 990 filed 2023.
notes: Established 1985 as the Philadelphia affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International. Has built 170+ homes and repaired 100+ in the city. Prior executive directors not surfaced in available sources.

name: Impact Services Corporation
statusReason: Filed Form 990 for FY ending June 2025 with ~$19.9M revenue and growing net assets; maintains a current website and named CEO.
notes: Founded 1974 in Kensington out of the Kensington Environmental Center via a Ford Foundation employment demonstration project; IRS tax-exempt ruling March 1982. Serves 17,000+ Philadelphians annually. Prior executive directors not surfaced.

name: New Kensington CDC
statusReason: Filed a Form 990 for FY ending June 2025 showing $9.9M revenue; opened a new Kensington Community Engagement Center in January 2025; current PACDC member with a maintained website.
notes: Founded 1985 to address housing needs in Kensington; tax-exempt status July 1985. Serves Kensington, Port Richmond, and Fishtown. Longtime ED Sandy Salzman retired in 2016 after ~21 years; successor Felix Torres-Colon (started March 2017) died in office in February 2020; Bill McKinney has led since 2020.

name: Overbrook West Neighbors CDC
statusReason: Appears on the City of Philadelphia's April 2026 Registered Community Organization list (designation expires 2027) with Gregory Allen as primary contact; current PACDC member with an active website; last 990 filed 2023.
notes: Founded and incorporated in 2018 as a grassroots Overbrook (West Philadelphia) effort focused on the Upper Lancaster Avenue Business Corridor. A smaller, largely volunteer/board-led organization rather than a staffed real estate CDC; no published staff executive director, leadership is a board plus a Neighborhood Action Committee. Gregory Allen is founder/president and the City's RCO contact.

name: Smart Futures CDC
statusReason: Live website at smartfutures.org with current programs; ongoing operations as a statewide career-planning platform nonprofit; last 990 filed 2023.
notes: EIN 30-0263715 (matches source). Nonprofit providing a statewide youth career-planning/portfolio platform; David Mosey is both founder and current Executive Director, founded 2005. Caveat: the org appears to be Pittsburgh-based (not a Philadelphia neighborhood CDC), which may be a misclassification in the source list. Prior/other executive directors not found (Mosey is founder).

name: Women’s Community Revitalization Project (WCRP)
statusReason: Live website (wcrpphila.org) showing 2026 content, open housing applications, and an active job posting; a Feb 13, 2026 Philadelphia Inquirer article reports WCRP under new leadership developing apartments on public land in Kensington.
notes: Philadelphia's first women-led community development organization; affordable-housing development, supportive services, and advocacy. Founding year most commonly cited as 1986 (some sources say 1985 or 1987). Founder Nora Lichtash led for ~35 years and retired in 2025; Lorissa Luciani took over as ED in 2025. No IRS/990 data was provided in the source; EIN appears in third-party profiles as 22-2840188.

name: Village of Arts and Humanities
statusReason: Website is live with recent stories/news and last 990 filed for 2023.
notes: Founded 1986 as Lily Yeh's North Philadelphia park-building project; formally incorporated in 1989 (per the org's About page). currentExec (Elmore-Stratton) departed 7/11/24; Melody Keim joined as Interim ED Jan 2025 (per LinkedIn/ZoomInfo). The org has shifted toward a leadership-team/co-executive model. ED years for Elmore-Stratton and Yeh are approximate; interim-ED detail comes from LinkedIn rather than the org's own team page.
